APPENDIX A – CONTRACT TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Official Product Name:
“Will an alternative wage for Californian goat herders be authorized <time period>?”
Rulebook:
CAGOATWAGE
CAGOATWAGE
Scope:
These rules shall apply to this contract.
Underlying:
The Underlying for this Contract is official records of the State of California and reporting from the Source

Agencies regarding legislative, regulatory, executive, and judicial actions affecting the minimum wage and overtime

obligations applicable to California employers of goat herders <time period>. Revisions to the Underlying made after

Expiration will not be accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.
Source Agency:
The Source Agencies are, in hierarchical order, California Legislative Information, the official journals of

the Assembly and Senate of California, the Office of the Governor of California, the California Secretary of State, the

California Department of Industrial Relations (including the Labor Commissioner/DLSE and the Industrial Welfare

Commission), the California Office of Administrative Law, the Official Californian Code of Regulations. the issuing court,

the Associated Press, Reuters, The Guardian, Bloomberg News, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The

Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, the San Francisco Chronicle, the Sacramento Bee, CalMatters, Politico, Axios,

CNN, ABC, CBS, NBC, Agri-Pulse, and Fox News.
Type:
The type of Contract is an Event Contract.
Issuance:
After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will be listed on an as-needed basis at the discretion of the Exchange

and corresponding to the risk management needs of Members.
<time period>:
<time period> refers to a specific duration or range of time as specified by the Exchange. May be

expressed as a calendar year (e.g., "2026"), a calendar month and year (e.g., "September 2026"), a calendar quarter (e.g., "Q3

2026"), a specific week, or other bounded time periods as appropriate to the contract subject matter. All time periods are

interpreted in Eastern Time (ET) unless otherwise specified. The end of <time period> is defined as 11:59:59 PM ET on the

final day of the specified period, unless otherwise specified. The Exchange may list iterations of the Contract corresponding

to variations of <time period>.
Payout Criterion:
The Payout Criterion for the Contract encompasses the Expiration Values that a Qualifying Action has

been taken <time period>.
A "Qualifying Action" means:
1.
a California statute has become law, whether by the Governor's signature, by passage over a gubernatorial veto under

Article IV, Section 10(a) of the California Constitution, or by operation of Article IV, Section 10(b), and regardless of

vehicle, including a policy bill, urgency statute, budget bill, budget trailer bill, or special session bill;
2.
a regulation finally approved by the California Office of Administrative Law and filed with the California Secretary of

State, or an Industrial Welfare Commission wage order that has been amended or republished and has taken effect;
3.
a written regulation, binding directive, final order, or formal statewide enforcement policy issued by a California state

agency, department, board, commission, or officer with authority over the subject matter, including but not limited to

the Department of Industrial Relations, the Labor Commissioner and the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement,

the Industrial Welfare Commission, the Employment Development Department, the Department of Food and

Agriculture, the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, and the Department of Finance. An opinion letter or

official interpretation is included only if it binds the issuing body or expressly states that body's statewide enforcement

position;
4.
an executive order or proclamation issued by the Governor of California; or
5.
a written order entered by a California state court or a United States federal court.

[page 2 of 5: text layer]
Which has at least one of the following effects:
1.
it reenacts, revives, restores, or extends the alternative monthly wage authority formerly contained in California

Labor Code Section 2695.4(a), or establishes an alternative to it;
a.
"Goat herder" means an individual employed to perform any of the duties described in former California

Labor Code Section 2695.3(d), as that section read immediately before its repeal on July 1, 2026. Where

an instrument described above defines goat herders or a comparable class differently, that instrument's

definition governs for purposes of applying the Payout Criterion to that instrument.
2.
it provides that goat herders are eligible for the alternative monthly wage framework applicable to sheepherders

under California Labor Code Sections 2695.1 and 2695.2, including by determining that "sheepherder" as used

in California Labor Code Section 2695.2 encompasses goat herders;
3.
it establishes an alternative monthly wage, a special minimum wage, a modified overtime threshold, a modified

compensable-hours rule, an exemption in whole or in part from minimum wage or overtime requirements, a safe

harbor, or a limitation on damages or penalties (subject to the conditions set out in what would NOT satisfy the

Payout Criterion), in each case applicable to goat herders or their employers;
4.
it directs that any portion of the minimum wage or overtime obligations otherwise applicable to California

employers of goat herders not be enforced or collected, including by a formal written policy of enforcement

forbearance;
5.
it provides employers of goat herders a tax credit, reimbursement, grant, subsidy, payment, or contract price

adjustment expressly tied to goat herder minimum wage or overtime obligations; or
6.
it enjoins or prohibits the enforcement or collection of any portion of the minimum wage or overtime

obligations otherwise applicable to California employers of goat herders, or declares those obligations wholly or

partially inapplicable to goat herders. A stay entered solely on procedural grounds, including arbitration, venue,

discovery, bankruptcy, or case management, is not a Qualifying Action unless the order itself bars enforcement

or collection of the underlying wage or overtime obligation.
And which:
1.
applies statewide, or is generally available to employers of goat herders as a class, and is not limited to a named

employer, a named individual, or the parties to an individual, non-class case;
2.
was enacted, approved and filed, issued, or entered, as applicable, on or before the end of <time period>;
3.
has qualifying provisions that have taken legal effect, or by their express terms apply to compensation for work

performed, on or before the end of <time period>;
4.
has qualifying provisions that have not been stayed, enjoined, suspended, invalidated, rescinded, or superseded

as of the Expiration Date at the Expiration time; and
5.
satisfies the Net Monthly Cost test described below.
Subject to the foregoing requirements, an instrument is a Qualifying Action whether its relief is partial or complete,

temporary or permanent, retroactive or prospective, and regardless of its label, vehicle, or stated duration.
Net Monthly Cost test.
An instrument satisfies the Net Monthly Cost test if the Net Monthly Cost under the

instrument does not exceed the monthly minimum wage applicable to sheepherders under California Labor Code

Section 2695.2 and Section 4(E) of Industrial Welfare Commission Wage Order No. 14-2001, plus 15%, as in effect

on the last day of <time period>. An instrument that enjoins or prohibits the enforcement or collection of the

applicable minimum wage and overtime obligations in their entirety is deemed to satisfy this test.
Net Monthly Cost means the employer's minimum required wage and overtime cost of compensating a goat herder

employed on a regularly scheduled 24-hour shift, seven days per week, for one calendar month, computed under the

wage and overtime rules as modified, limited, or rendered unenforceable by the instrument, minus the monthly value

of any credit, reimbursement, grant, subsidy, payment, or contract price adjustment legally available to the employer

under the instrument.
Where and to the extent the goat herder's compensation is determined under hourly wage and overtime rules, the

[page 3 of 5: text layer]
following defaults apply, except to the extent the instrument itself legally modifies the number of compensable hours,

the applicable hourly wage rate, or the applicable premium pay requirements, in which case the instrument's modified

terms govern: all 24 hours of each shift are treated as compensable; the applicable rate is the California minimum

wage in effect on the last day of <time period>; each workweek consists of 40 hours at the regular rate, 40 hours at

one and one half times the regular rate, and 88 hours at two times the regular rate; and one calendar month equals

52/12 workweeks.
Only benefits available as of right to all qualifying employers, without further appropriation, competitive award,

application ranking, or agency discretion, are included in the computation. A lump sum benefit is prorated over the

period to which it is expressly attributable, and a benefit that cannot be allocated on a per goat herder, per month basis

is not included. An instrument consisting of a written order entered by a California state court or a United States

federal court is tested by computing Net Monthly Cost under the obligations as limited by that instrument.
The legal date of an instrument controls, and not the date on which it is published, posted, or reported. A statute is dated as of

the date it becomes law; a regulation as of final approval by the Office of Administrative Law and filing with the Secretary

of State, or as of another legally controlling adoption date; a wage order as of its stated effective date; an administrative

directive, final order, or formal statewide enforcement position as of its official issuance; an executive order or proclamation

as of its issuance; and a court order as of its entry.
The following do not satisfy the Payout Criterion:
a bill that has not become law, including a bill passed by one or both chambers and a bill vetoed and not overridden;
a proposed regulation, rulemaking notice, petition, or draft policy that has not been finally approved and filed;
the filing or pendency of litigation without a written order of a California state court or a United States federal court;
a nonbinding advisory, an opinion letter that neither binds the issuing body nor expressly states that body's statewide

enforcement position, a staff communication, a frequently-asked-questions page, or a website statement;
a statement, press release, hearing, study, report, recommendation, or political agreement;
an authorization of a future program that requires a further appropriation, implementing legislation, or discretionary

agency approval before relief becomes legally available;
a general appropriation or funding for agriculture, grazing, fire prevention, or vegetation management not expressly

tied to goat herder minimum wage or overtime obligations;
a reenactment limited to the definitional, housing, meal period, safety, communication, transportation, or other non-
wage provisions formerly contained in California Labor Code Sections 2695.3 and 2695.4;
federal legislation and federal executive or administrative action, provided that a written order of a United States

federal court is not excluded by this item;
action by a city, county, fire district, or other local government, unless it implements a qualifying state program;
a private settlement or agreement not entered as a written order of a California state court or a United States federal

court;
and relief consisting solely of a limitation on damages, penalties, or interest, without any of (a) any reduction of

the underlying wage, (b) any reduction of overtime obligation, OR (c) any qualifying payment.
Only actions documented by a Source Agency on or before the Expiration Date at the Expiration time will be considered.

Where the records of the Source Agencies conflict, or where a Source Agency retracts, corrects, or removes information, the

official records of the body that took the action govern.
Examples that would resolve the market to Yes:
<time period> is "August 2026." On August 28, 2026, the Legislature passes and the Governor signs an urgency statute

making goat herders eligible for the alternative monthly wage authorized for sheepherders by Labor Code Section

2695.2, effective immediately. The statute is not stayed, enjoined, suspended, or invalidated as of the Expiration Date

at the Expiration time. The Net Monthly Cost under the alternative monthly wage does not exceed the Net Monthly

Cost test threshold.
<time period> is "September 2026." On September 25, 2026, the Governor signs a bill authorizing employers of goat

[page 4 of 5: text layer]
herders to pay, in lieu of the minimum wage for all hours worked, a monthly wage of no less than $5,200, by its

express terms applicable to compensation for work performed on and after July 1, 2026. The monthly minimum wage

applicable to sheepherders in effect on September 30, 2026 is $4,938.21, so the Net Monthly Cost test threshold is

$5,678.94, and the bill's $5,200 Net Monthly Cost does not exceed it.
<time period> is "Q3 2026." On August 20, 2026, the Industrial Welfare Commission amends and republishes Wage

Order No. 14-2001 to provide that a goat herder employed on a regularly scheduled 24-hour, seven-day-per-week on-
call shift is compensable for eight hours per day, effective on that date. The Net Monthly Cost computed under the

amended wage order does not exceed the Net Monthly Cost test threshold.
<time period> is "2026." On November 10, 2026, a California superior court enters a written order in a certified class

action declaring that goat herders statewide are eligible for the alternative monthly wage framework applicable to

sheepherders under Labor Code Section 2695.2. The order is in effect as of the Expiration Date at the Expiration time.

The Net Monthly Cost under the alternative monthly wage does not exceed the Net Monthly Cost test threshold.
Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:
<time period> is "August 2026." The Senate passes a goat herder wage parity bill on August 25, 2026, but the

Assembly does not act on it, and no such bill becomes law on or before August 31, 2026.
<time period> is "2026." On September 15, 2026, the Governor signs a bill appropriating $10,000,000 to the

Department of Forestry and Fire Protection for targeted grazing contracts, and no instrument produces any of the

effects listed above on or before December 31, 2026.
<time period> is "Q3 2026." On August 5, 2026, the Labor Commissioner posts a frequently-asked-questions page on

the Department of Industrial Relations website stating that the office does not currently intend to prioritize

enforcement actions against goat-grazing employers, and no instrument produces any of the effects listed above on or

before September 30, 2026.
<time period> is "2026." On September 20, 2026, the Governor signs a bill authorizing employers of goat herders to

pay, in lieu of the minimum wage for all hours worked, a monthly wage of no less than $12,000. The monthly

minimum wage applicable to sheepherders in effect on December 31, 2026 is $4,938.21, so the Net Monthly Cost test

threshold is $5,678.94, and the bill's $12,000 Net Monthly Cost exceeds it. No other instrument produces a qualifying

effect on or before December 31, 2026.
<time period> is "2026." On October 2, 2026, a California superior court enters an order in a wage claim brought by

one goat herder against one employer holding that the employer may compensate that goat herder on a monthly basis.

The order is limited to the parties to that individual, non-class case.
Minimum Tick:
The Minimum Tick size for the Contract shall be $0.01.
Position Accountability Level:
The Position Accountability Level for the Contract shall be $25,000 per strike, per

Member.
Last Trading Date:
The Last Trading Date of the Contract will be the same as the Expiration Date. The Last Trading Time

will be the same as the Expiration time.
Settlement Date:
The Settlement Date of the Contract shall be no later than the day after the Expiration Date, unless the

Market Outcome is under review pursuant to Rule 7.1.
Expiration Date:
The latest Expiration Date of the Contract shall be one week after the end of <time period>. If an event

described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance with Rule 7.2.
Expiration time:
The Expiration time of the Contract shall be 10:00 AM ET.
Settlement Value:
The Settlement Value for this Contract is $1.00.
Expiration Value:
The Expiration Value is the value of the Underlying as documented by the Source Agency on the

Expiration Date at the Expiration time.

[page 5 of 5: text layer]
Contingencies:
Before Settlement, Kalshi may, at its sole discretion, initiate the Market Outcome Review Process pursuant

to Rule 7.1 of the Rulebook. If an Expiration Value cannot be determined on the Expiration Date, Kalshi has the right to

determine payouts pursuant to Rule 7.1 in the Rulebook.
APPENDIX B – TRADING PROHIBITIONS
In addition to the general prohibition against trading on material nonpublic information, the Exchange will institute additional

prohibitions for trading the contract. Persons under 18 years of age are not permitted to create Kalshi accounts. The

following individuals will be prohibited from trading:
Members, officers, and employees of the California State Senate and State Assembly, including committee, leadership,

and Rules Committee staff, the Office of Legislative Counsel, the Legislative Analyst's Office, and the Chief Clerk's

and Senate Secretary's offices.
The Governor and the Governor's office legislative-affairs and legal-affairs staff; officers and employees of the

Department of Finance, the Office of Administrative Law, and the Secretary of State personnel responsible for

chaptering enrolled bills.
Officers and employees of the Department of Industrial Relations, the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement and

the Labor Commissioner's office, the Industrial Welfare Commission, the Employment Development Department, the

Department of Food and Agriculture, and the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, in each case where the

individual has authority over or advance knowledge of wage-order or enforcement-policy actions affecting goat

herders.
Lobbyists registered with the California Secretary of State on this subject matter, together with their employers and

clients; officers and staff of the California Farm Bureau Federation, the California Wool Growers Association, the

California Cattlemen's Association, the California Labor Federation, and the United Farm Workers.
Counsel of record, party representatives, named plaintiffs, class representatives, expert witnesses, and court personnel

in any pending or threatened action seeking an order that would satisfy the Payout Criterion.
Any person retained to draft or negotiate proposed statutory or regulatory language on this subject, including officers,

directors, and employees of California goat-grazing and targeted-grazing contractors participating in that drafting or

negotiation.
Immediate family members and members of the household of any person listed above.
